clue.text: New suit, but it's no replacement

indicators.note: new here means made afresh, so the letters of the following words are reworked

parts.note: the contraction gives its three letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists a freshly bought suit is no substitute for the old one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like an adjective on 'suit' but signals the anagram of SUIT BUT ITS NO; the clue even claims the result is 'no replacement' when it is exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute player or item is put in place of another, the act of swapping one for another.

clue.text: Defence against the main onslaught

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the sea, so this is a barrier against the waves battering a coast

explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' reads as 'the principal onslaught' in battle, but in crosswords and poetry the main is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal barrier of masonry built to stop the waves eroding the land.

clue.text: Awfully noisy sportsman about 50, a social worker

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the sportsman's word goes around the number

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket, a sporting player
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
an ant is a worker insect living in a colony, hence social

explanation.surface: A loud athlete of around fifty takes up social work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a welfare officer, but crosswords use it for the ant, which lives in organised colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: In its older sense the word means loud and clamorous, offensively so.

clue.text: Will examine before midday — before ten possibly

parts.note: to test is to examine
a.m. is ante meridiem, the hours before noon

indicators.note: possibly says the word ten may appear in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone will hold an exam in the morning, perhaps before ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like the auxiliary verb but is the noun, a legal document; 'possibly' turns TEN into ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document disposing of a person's estate after death.

clue.text: Sent up thus in play or opera

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the letters are written from the bottom upwards, so read backwards
in places the word for thus inside the word for a play

parts.note: an act is part of a play, standing for the drama
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A play or opera is mocked, sent up in a parody.
explanation.walkthrough: SO goes inside ACT to make ACSOT, and 'Sent up' turns it over, as befits a down light. 'Sent up' hints at parody, but it means reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's Tosca is a famous Italian opera about a singer, a painter and a police chief.

clue.text: Leaflet in support of climber

parts.note: in botany a leaflet can be modified into a slender coiling thread that holds a climbing plant up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaflet' suggests a pamphlet backing a mountaineer, but it is a small leaf part on a plant that clings to its support.
explanation.definitionFit: A modified leaf or stem that coils round supports, helping vines and peas to climb.

clue.text: Sea Islands — a Pacific group

parts.note: an ocean is a great sea
I is an abbreviation for island, as on maps

explanation.surface: A geography note naming a chain of islands in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: The region taking in Australia, New Zealand and the scattered Pacific island nations.

clue.text: Representative, a stable man, without a seat?

parts.note: a stand-in represents or deputises for someone else
a groom looks after horses in a stable

explanation.surface: A deputy who works in the stables finds himself with nowhere to sit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: space for people who have no seat at a theatre or match, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Space at a venue where spectators stand because all the seats are taken.

clue.text: Plenty to drink?

parts.note: bags means plenty in British slang, and these are bags holding a drink's leaves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags of' is British slang for lots of; here the bags literally hold something for brewing a hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Small porous sachets of dried leaves steeped in hot water to brew a cuppa.

clue.text: Not naturally bright

parts.note: reads as dim-witted, but describes a place with no daylight from the sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not naturally bright' sounds like an insult to someone's intelligence; it means lacking light from nature's own source.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no daylight at all, dark and gloomy for want of the star in our sky.

clue.text: He has to make certain set changes

definitions.text: He has to make certain set changes

parts.words: He has to make certain set changes
parts.note: a set here is theatre scenery, which a stagehand moves between scenes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Set changes' sounds like adjustments to a fixed arrangement, but a theatre set is scenery moved by stage crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagehand whose job is moving theatre scenery between acts.

clue.text: Falls back again, meeting men with guns.

indicators.note: back means the word again is read in reverse order

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: Someone falls back once more and runs into armed men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like a verb but is the noun, a waterfall; 'back' turns AGAIN into NIAGA.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterfalls on the US-Canada border are the best-known example of a cataract.

clue.text: A right to extend file

parts.note: to range is to extend or stretch over an area

explanation.surface: An instruction that one has the right to lengthen a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'File' reads as a noun, a document, but it is the verb meaning put in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To file papers is to put them in order, sorting them systematically.

clue.text: An opening for a boatman.

parts.note: sounds like a job vacancy for a sailor, but is a gap in a coastline a boat may enter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' suggests a job going; it is a literal opening in the shore, a small bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow arm of the sea or a creek running into the land.

clue.text: Peel off from back of one in last minute

parts.note: ex is Latin for from, as in ex-works

indicators.note: back says the little word of is read the other way round
in says the numeral for one goes inside the words for last minute

parts.note: late means at the last minute
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Instructions to strip something away at the very last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of one' reads as the last letter of 'one', but 'back' reverses OF to give FO; 'in' puts I into LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed or remove dead skin or bark in flakes or scales.

clue.text: Constituents forget his looking ahead

indicators.note: constituents are component parts, so the letters of the two words are the parts to rebuild from

explanation.surface: Voters ignore an MP's planning for the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituents' suggests voters in a constituency, but it signals the parts of FORGET HIS to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Planning ahead or anticipating what the future will need.

clue.text: There can be no greater energy-giver

indicators.note: can be says the letters of these words can become another arrangement

explanation.surface: A boast that no source of power could be finer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface claims nothing greater exists; read cryptically, NO GREATER can become a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine such as a dynamo that turns mechanical motion into electrical power.

clue.text: Planet provides rising writer with theme

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is written upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a tune is a musical theme

explanation.surface: A planet inspires an up-and-coming author with a subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising writer' suggests an up-and-coming author; in a down light it turns PEN into NEP. 'Theme' is musical here.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth and outermost major body orbiting our sun, named after the Roman sea god.

clue.text: The intention is to separate

definitions.meaning: to break down into component parts, as light into colours

explanation.surface: A declaration that the plan is a parting of ways.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a firm determination or purpose; as a verb, to break something down into its component parts.

clue.text: Slope where game may be seen

definitions.meaning: the degree of incline, as of a roof
a sports ground on which a match is played

explanation.surface: A hillside where hunters might spot animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' suggests wild animals on a hillside, but it is a sports match on a playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof's slope or gradient; and a sports field on which a match is played.

clue.text: It may be inapt to serve guinea-fowl

indicators.note: may be says the letters of inapt may become another word

parts.note: to do for someone is to serve them, so do means serve

explanation.surface: Serving guinea-fowl might be inappropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inapt' rearranged gives PINTA; 'serve' gives DO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a name for a type of guinea-fowl, from the Portuguese word for painted, after its speckled plumage.

clue.text: Companies of soldiers, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for soldiers is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: troops are soldiers

explanation.surface: A remark that companies are made up of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Companies of soldiers' looks like one military phrase; 'Companies' is the definition, of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of touring actors, dancers or entertainers are theatrical companies.

clue.text: Faced with work, sat still

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
to pose is to sit still for a portrait

explanation.surface: Someone confronted with a job just sat motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faced' means set against or confronting.
explanation.definitionFit: Set against something or confronted by an opponent.

clue.text: Foreign currency row with a revolutionary leader

parts.note: a din is a noisy row or racket

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A dispute over foreign money involves a rebel chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is a noisy quarrel, rhyming with cow, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The monetary unit of several countries, including Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait and Serbia.

clue.text: Dispatch some letters — end of Friday's business

indicators.note: some says only a run of letters is taken from the words that follow, spanning the dash

explanation.surface: Sending off some post as the last of Friday's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the final S of 'letters' and ends at the F of 'Friday's'; 'business' only rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell party or ceremony for someone leaving.

clue.text: Tearful girl having brought back nothing

parts.note: Maud is a girl's name

indicators.note: brought back says the word for nothing is reversed

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A girl weeps because she returned empty-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns NIL into LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-pityingly or sentimentally weepy, especially when drunk.

clue.text: King should be followed by a couple of pages, the French contend

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George, seen on British postboxes
p is the abbreviation for page, so two of them give pp
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Royal instructions: two young attendants follow the king to fight the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pages' suggests young royal attendants; here P is page in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple with a problem or opponent is to struggle or wrestle with it.

clue.text: Put a variety of rice on tables for the festivities

indicators.note: a variety means a mix, so the letters of the three words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Lay out various rice dishes on the tables for the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' is a link; 'a variety of' rearranges RICE ON TABLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Parties and festive events marking a happy occasion.
